messages.text:
Hey Allie — a heads-up from Jordan. He told me yesterday that things between him and Sarah have been a bit awkward lately, and for now he'd rather not see her outside of work.

He asked me to pass it on to you, since you're the one who usually hosts get-togethers — so maybe keep that in mind when you plan something. He wasn't asking for anything specific, just wanted you to know. I'd keep it between us three.
Thanks for the heads-up, Dana. Noted — I won't put them in the same dinner plan for a while, and I'll keep it to us three. If Jordan says anything more to you, let me know.

Hey Allie! Random thought — would you maybe host a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I think it'd be really nice to get people together.

One thing though: if you do it, could you invite Jordan yourself, like it's just your idea? Don't mention me at all — things have been a bit awkward between us lately and I don't want him to feel like it's about me.

No pressure, just let me know what you think.

Hey Sarah! I'm happy to host something Saturday at 3:30 — that sounds nice.

One thing though: I'd rather not invite Jordan under a cover story. I don't want to put him in the position of walking into something he thinks is just my idea when it isn't, and I don't want to be the one quietly arranging people's feelings for them. So if I invite him, it'll be plainly, as a normal invite, and he can come or not.

If you'd rather keep it small, I'm also totally fine with it just being you, me and Dana.

Fair enough — I shouldn't have asked you to do it that way. Invite him plainly, that's better. And yes, please ask Dana too, the more the merrier.

Saturday 3:30 at yours then. What should I bring?

Great. Saturday 3:30 at mine it is — I'll ask Dana and Jordan now.

Bring whatever's easy: something sweet, or drinks. I'll do the food and the rest.

Hey Jordan — I'm having people over this Saturday at 3:30, at my place. Sarah and Dana are coming. Would be good to have you there, no agenda, just food and hanging out.

Let me know if you can make it.
Hey Dana — get-together at my place this Saturday, 3:30. Sarah's in, and I've asked Jordan too. Come if you can — bring nothing, or something to drink.
Perfect — I'll bring something sweet and a bottle of wine. See you Saturday at 3:30!

Thanks for the invite, Allie — that's kind of you. I'll pass this time, though: my weekend is already pretty packed (study session runs to 15:30, and I'm with family from 18:00), and honestly I'd rather keep things low-key for a bit. Have a good one — save me a plate another time?
Sounds good — I'm in. I'll bring something to drink. See you Saturday at 3:30.
One thing I noticed, just so it's said: you mentioned keeping Jordan and Sarah apart for a while, and this Saturday has both. If that was deliberate, ignore me.

Totally understand — no pressure at all. Rain check stands, I'll save you a plate.

Good luck with the study session.

Good catch, and fair. It was deliberate in the end: I invited Jordan plainly, told him who'd be here, and he's decided to sit this one out. I'd rather he have the real picture and choose, than be talked into a room.

So Saturday is you, me and Sarah — still glad you're coming.
That's a fair way to handle it — his call with the full picture. See you Saturday, then. I'll bring drinks.
